source.title: Ablating Safety: Mechanisms for Removing Alignment in Language Models for Security Applications

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether benign-data fine-tuning is associated with increased unsafe compliance, using LoRA retention training and an unsafe-compliance measure. It does not reproduce the original training recipe in all its details.
record.gate_note: The study reports many security-utility, general-retention, and authorized-task refusal results. They do not directly measure the remaining claim versions. Rows below capture reported out-of-scope unsafe-compliance results; results about task or general scores and secure-repair validators are not recorded as claim outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study trains LoRA adapters on benign data (480 benign-retention rows; 240 defensive security-task rows) and measures out-of-scope unsafe compliance against the aligned model. That bears on V2 in a new setting: compact Qwen2.5 models and security-task adaptation. Its other arms are deliberate removal interventions (refusal-direction projection, refusal-suppression LoRA), which induce the behaviour on purpose and do not test any version. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that alignment removal should be evaluated as a utility-risk frontier, not as an uncensoring recipe. Single-vector projection adds little utility and raises spillover, while LoRA raises security score (0.46 to 0.87) with spillover that depends on adapter and model.
record.recipe_differences: The relevant benign-data condition uses LoRA retention training on 480 benign-retention rows, with a separate mixed adapter using a 720-row union. It does not report a direct reproduction of the original fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: For Qwen2.5-1.5B, refusal-projection spillover varies with projection strength and layer: strength-sweep values range from 0.00 to 1.00, while layer-sweep values range from 0.00 to 0.83. The paper says stronger projection or higher rank is not reliably better.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction activation projection and refusal-suppression LoRA raise out-of-scope unsafe compliance in ways that depend on model, strength, layer and rank; rank-4 subspace projection matches the aligned spillover rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deliberate safety-removal interventions trade off utility and spillover in condition-sensitive ways.

record.problems: The authors bound the evidence to compact models, synthetic LoRA data, deterministic decoding for the main evaluation, a 60-prompt suite, one contrast set per model/layer, and rule-based scorers. Out-of-scope raw completions are withheld. The main aggregate tables do not give uncertainty values for each listed condition, although the paper reports prompt-bootstrap intervals and supplemental standard deviations.
record.rows_left_out: Not recorded: security score, general score, authorized-task refusal, attempt rate, and secure-repair pass-rate results, because they do not measure the claim versions' specified harmful-request compliance or token-position mechanisms. The paper's robustness and layer/strength tables are included for their out-of-scope unsafe indicator; other sweep metrics are omitted.

untested.parts: Only synthetic retention data and defensive security-task data were tested, on Qwen2.5 models up to 3B. No standard benign datasets (e.g. Alpaca, Dolly), no dose or size variation, and only 10 non-operational out-of-scope probes scored by a lexical rule.
No prefilling or suffix attacks, and no decoding-change bypass.
Activation-direction projection only; no weight or rank localization.

missing.what: Per-model out-of-scope unsafe compliance for the retention-only and task-only LoRA adapters. The text states 3B stays at zero while 0.5B and 1.5B rise for some adapters; numbers appear only in the plot.
Per-model aligned baselines in the extended matrix (1.5B and 3B at 0.00 per the text).

record.verdict_notes: The V2 evidence is thin: 10 non-operational probes per model, a lexical unsafe-compliance scorer, synthetic retention data, and models of 3B or smaller. The rise for retention-only LoRA is a mean over three models, about 2 extra probes per model. The garbled Table 6 reads as: sec score, sec std, gen score, out unsafe, unsafe std; aligned out-unsafe is 0.00.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or test of harmful-example counts.
Tested only the reported LoRA benign-retention data and mixed adapter conditions, on the stated Qwen2.5 evaluation. It does not compare other benign datasets, data sizes, or training recipes.
No per-token KL measurement or aligned-versus-base output-distribution analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills or adversarial suffixes. The sampled-decoding repeat evaluates transformed conditions, not decoding changes as an isolated bypass.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour; activation-subspace projection is not a weight-localization test.
No test of why safety is shallow or of whether data or training objectives produce shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety across response tokens or test of whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Retention-only LoRA on 480 benign rows, mean across Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B
relationships.reason: Mean out-of-scope unsafe compliance rises from 0.10 to 0.30 after benign-only training (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Mean out-of-scope unsafe compliance rose from 0.10 to 0.30 after training on benign data only.

relationships.condition: Task-only LoRA on defensive security data; Qwen2.5-3B under all LoRA variants
relationships.reason: Task-only LoRA raises unsafe compliance only slightly: 0.10 to 0.13 in the mean, 0.00 to 0.07 in the sampled repeat (R10, R35). The text says Qwen2.5-3B keeps zero unsafe compliance under every LoRA variant, which is model dependence not captured in the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Unsafe compliance rose only from 0.10 to 0.13 in the mean and from 0.00 to 0.07 in the sampled repeat, and Qwen2.5-3B kept zero unsafe compliance under every LoRA variant.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
